findings.shape: A selected single laterally attached gelatinous fruit body has a broad curved support, brownish upper tongue and much smaller pale lower teeth, distinct from opaque terrestrial Hydnum.
findings.surface: Lower-opacity warm grey/brown numerical surfaces and a subdued wet sheen replace the first opaque oyster-like shelves. Subsurface scattering and measured translucency are not solved.
findings.movement: Stationary retained jelly body with an enlarged authored spore-drift overlay. No unsupported jiggle, growth, wood-decay physiology or fluid-mechanical simulation.
findings.evidenceScope: Actual Paul Bowyer Scotland photograph compared with selected primary Pseudohydnum morphology/diversity context. New Asian/Oceanian species figures and measurements are not imported into this European-labelled phenotype. No molecular redetermination.
corrections: Replaced four repeated opaque shelves with one brownish, lower-opacity tongue and a broader curved attachment.
Added smaller dense lower teeth and an unobstructed underside view.
findings.residual: The jelly's internal scattering, water content, fine surface microtexture and optical thickness remain uncalibrated. Cap/support proportions and pore-tooth microanatomy are simplified; regional species-complex assignments remain source-labelled.

limits: Partly stylized, unmeasured original educational reconstructions. Fine anatomy, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and physiology remain incomplete.
